We delivered strong performance in Q3, including organic growth of 3.3%,
operating margin of 26.2%, up 110 basis points,
earnings per share of $2.50, up 12%,
and free cash flow of $1.2 billion.
We returned $600 million to shareholders in the past year,

These results include Madison Fire and Rescue,
which is now fully consolidated into our financial reporting
and reflect a change in acquisition amortization reporting.
Our updated guidance for the year incorporates both items,
and OnRog will provide additional details later in the call.
Based on our Q3 performance and continued strong order trends,
we remain transparent.
We are confident in achieving organic growth of greater than 3.5% this year.
The progress we're delivering reflects the disciplined execution
of the strategy we've been implementing over the last two years.
As we've discussed, a value creation framework is centered around three phases,
building the foundation, driving transformation, and accelerating performance.
Our results today are clear evidence that we're making progress across all three.
We're strengthening the foundation,
and we're building critical capabilities to position 3M for long-term success.
We've invested in Salesforce effectiveness and AI-enabled tools.
We've sharpened our focus on priority verticals where we can win,
and improved how we allocate R&D resources.
Operationally, we're delivering on our goals to improve productivity,
quality, and supply chain performance.
In the quarter, we launched 87 new products,
up 24%, and we're on track to exceed our target of 350 this year.
Year-to-date, five-year new product sales are up 34% versus last year to nearly $3 billion,
resulting in new product vitality in the mid-teens from a low of 11% in 2024.
Cross-selling is also gaining traction, with $140 million in wins booked to date,
and another $120 million in the pipeline, well ahead of our original target,
which is $1.5 billion.
And in today's higher inflation environment,
our price execution has been particularly strong,
and fully offsets material and oil cost pressures.
Across our manufacturing and supply chain network,
productivity improvements including procurement savings,
higher asset utilization from increased throughput and lower downtime,
and improved quality drove gross margins up 230 basis points year-over-year.
Cost support quality improved by 40 basis points,
and overall equipment effectiveness improved by 20 basis points.
We continue to see meaningful opportunities to further simplify and standardize,
reshape the portfolio, reduce risk, and improve enterprise resilience and predictability.
We've closed 16 manufacturing sites and distribution centers year-to-date,
and are taking action on 10 more over the next 12 months,
supporting further gross margin improvement beyond 2027.
And the Madison Fire and Rescue acquisition,
which is now combined with our SCBA business and reported as a separate division within SIPG,
is off to a good start.
The JV delivered high single-digit pro forma growth,
and operating margins ahead of our deal model and 3M overall,
and integration is well underway to capture synergies across distribution,
international expansion, and operational performance.
And we continue our efforts to address litigation risk,
and are actively working with a court-appointed mediator for the AFFF Personal Injury MDL,
and more information is available in our quarterly filing.
Moving to slide 4, I'll provide a bit more color on our end market performance.
We continue to see strong momentum in general industrial and safety,
with second half growth accelerating to high single digits,
above our prior expectations.
In electronics, we're seeing increasing strength in semiconductors and data centers,
which is partially offsetting a weaker consumer electronics market,
especially in LCD displays.
Auto OE and aftermarket is trending in line with prior expectations,
with a modest improvement from down low single digits in the first half,
to about flat in the second,
and with OE a bit softer,
and aftermarket a bit better.
The consumer business, which contributes about 20% of sales,
improves sequentially to about flat in the second half,
as modest improvement in consumer POS spending
is partially offset by channel inventory adjustments at a few specific retailers.
Net-net, we still see sales accelerating the second half,
and are full year above 3.5% organic.

to highlight the progress we're making.

greater durability,
and higher density optical connections for AI infrastructure.

including optical backplanes,
where connectors at the back of a server rack
can be difficult to access, install, and maintain.
We previously announced a partnership and deployment with Microsoft,
and said we were also engaged in proof of concept work
with five additional global hyposcalers,

Last evening, we filed an AK stating we issued a warrant to Amazon
to purchase up to 3.2 million shares,
or approximately 0.6% of 3M common stock,
based upon the achievement of $6 billion in cumulative sales of optical connectors,
and other data center-related products over the next seven years,
and other event-based milestones.
We also announced that we signed a contract manufacturing agreement
with Genius Electronic Optical Company, or GSEO,
and acquired a 4.7% stake in the company
in a private placement to cement our strategic partnership.
GSEO is a credible and proven supplier of premium consumer device components,
and they will help us rapidly advance technology development
and scale EBO manufacturing on top of our internal capacity expansion plans.
But as we previously said,
success in this space requires building a robust ecosystem of partners.
We're actively supporting industry standardization
through the EBO Multi-Source Agreement,
which started with 17 members and is now up to 63.
This MSA brings together hyperscalers,
connectivity providers,
and chip designers under a common framework
to establish industry standards and certify practitioners.
EBO was highlighted by many of these ecosystem partners
at last week's Open Compute Project Global Summit,
including by one other hyperscaler
demonstrating EBO in a next-gen rack design running live traffic,
and it was headlined in a recent article by Semi Analysis,
a well-respected trade journal.
We believe the combination of industry collaboration through the MSA,
growing ecosystem adoption,
and differentiated 3M know-how positions us well to benefit
as EBO becomes a larger part of next-generation AI infrastructure.
Overall, we've made meaningful progress
in reinvigorating our innovation engine over the last two years.
Success requires speed and precise execution,
and we're building a stronger,
faster, more innovative, and more resilient 3M.
As this company-wide effort evolves,
I'm confident it will translate into faster growth,
higher margins, and stronger free cash flow over time.
